coprime_steps_inspected: The finite residue formula supplies a primitive of one for the normalized derivation; no original-derivation primitive is asserted.
Constant lower-flow coefficients are admitted by the primary p43 remark, and coprimeness makes the leading J^m eigenvalues distinct.
Companion spectral coefficients are polynomial in the spectral parameter, so the original systems and fundamental-matrix inverses are ordinary at every finite spectral point.
The full formal phase is matched, including constant integration coefficients; matching only Stokes matrices would omit a necessary normalization.
Equal right jumps cancel in the left ratio. Its entire first row is exactly (1,0,...,0); x-derivatives identify all companion rows on the common local domain.

Formal phase coefficients lie in the algebraic field and have zero normalized derivative. Canonical sectorial solutions vary analytically locally, with constant Stokes matrices along finite continuation loops.
Trivial finite branch monodromy followed by Riemann-Hurwitz forces the coefficient field to be rational in the normalized time.
The positive infinity weight, strict derivative/lower-flow loss, and common-power polynomial conclusion give the stated coprime contradiction.
selfadjoint_steps_inspected: Skew projection has odd order, hence coprime to 2^e unless it has order one.
Finite fractional-flow subtraction puts centralizers of the resulting Airy form in C[w][E]; the polynomial shear gives C[P].
Leading coefficients descend the polynomial subtraction to the original constant field.
The valuation argument is applied in the original differential ring with a stable maximal ideal, independently of poles in the generic normalization.
